Rejects 'when two truths disagree, choose the better one' as an architectural primitive, replacing it with Detect->Contextualize->Classify->Preserve->Investigate->Resolve when authorized, and states 'conflict is not necessarily failure' (may represent genuine uncertainty, changing reality, different scopes/meanings, correction, competing expert interpretations, or unresolved organizational knowledge).

Sharpens the earlier Conflict!=Error invariant into a precise five-way chain: Difference!=Contradiction, Contradiction!=Correction, Correction!=Change, Change!=Recontextualization, and separately Superseded!=False (a superseded policy may remain historically valid while no longer currently applicable). For genuine same-context/same-time contradictions, requires preserving Conflict(P1,P2) rather than immediately choosing a winner, then investigating evidence strength, authority, context/timestamp/scope differences, or whether one is a correction, per the Step-181 conflict-classification criteria.

States the foundational move: no actor (engineer, team, server, CMDB, repository) literally owns a truth like 'the production server runs RHEL 9.8'; actors instead hold responsibility for establishing/maintaining it, authority to determine it, or accountability for acting on it -- 'truth itself is not an organizational ownership object.' Organizations own determinations, records, decisions, responsibilities, and governance processes, never truth itself; deconstructs 'single source of truth' into three incompatible meanings, only the second (one system authoritative for a particular fact) generally defensible.

Formalizes authority as proposition-specific: a monitoring system is authoritative for CurrentCPUUsage, the Architecture Board's record for ApprovedArchitecture, change-management for ProductionChangeAuthorization -- Authority(Source,P1) may differ from Authority(Source,P2), so 'there is no universal authoritative source', only sources authoritative for specific propositions/purposes. Grounds this in DDD (Customer means differently in Sales vs Billing; both meanings must be preserved), requiring proposition tuple P=<Meaning,Context,Scope,Time> so authority is evaluated as Authority(Source,P), stronger than a bare source.authoritative flag.

Introduces 'epistemic debt' by analogy to technical debt: a decision with Rationale=Unknown may represent debt, but only if the information was NotRecorded and important -- genuinely Indeterminate information incurs no debt -- formalized (as a research model, not a production metric) EpistemicDebt = Importance x Recoverability x Missingness. Extends Step 182's GovernanceAuthority!=EpistemicAuthority to GovernanceValidity != EpistemicCompleteness (a decision can be Valid AND PoorlyDocumented, so incomplete rationale does not automatically invalidate a decision). Proposes each proposition carry multiple orthogonal dimensions rather than one truth score: P=<Content,Context,Time,Provenance,EpistemicStatus,GovernanceStatus,Authority>, sketched further as a conceptual KnowledgeAssertion model (proposition/boundedContext/temporalScope/provenance/epistemicStatus/authorityContext/governanceStatus/relations), not yet a database schema.

Proposes Step 186, asking who is authorized to perform each specific epistemic-state transition (AI: Candidate->Supported? developer: Supported->Determined? Architecture Board: Determined->Decision? automated system: Decision->Action?), and specifically whether mere database write access constitutes authority to change organizational knowledge -- the author strongly suspects No, connecting this directly to the Permission->Power gap explicitly flagged as unresolved in the 1-182 alignment review, and to epistemic authority, governance authority, and technical permission more broadly.

Establishes three distinct epistemic conditions: Established (E |- P), Inferable (E,A |- P under explicit assumptions A), Unknown (E does not entail P and no justified inference closes the gap) -- Established != Inferable != Unknown, proposed as fundamental. Worked example: a 2026 migration approval with evidence but no recorded rationale must be represented as Rationale=Unknown, with any AI explanation kept as a separately labelled Hypothesis, never conflated with HistoricalReason.

Discovers there is no single knowledge graph but at least five distinct graphs with irreducibly different edge semantics -- Evidence (G_E: what supports what), Semantic (G_S: what means/refines/contradicts what), Temporal (G_T), Governance (G_G: who is authorized to decide what), Causal (G_C: what caused what) -- consolidated into a multilayer graph bold-G=(G_E,G_S,G_T,G_G,G_C), with the principle that different relation semantics require different graph interpretations (an evidence edge does not imply a governance edge; a governance-authority edge does not imply an edge to the truth of a proposition), called 'much more faithful to DDD than a single knowledge graph' and 'a major architectural result.'

Carefully reapplies the Gita continuity lens (explicitly without theological claim) to derive the precise question 'does a current state intrinsically contain its entire historical identity?', answered No and formalized KS_t does not imply {KS_0,...,KS_{t-1}}, giving CurrentState != HistoricalTrajectory, requiring external Lineage(KS_t) preservation. Models the 'Krishna knows' analogy as Observer_current seeing only KS_t while a higher-order observer with complete lineage sees T(KS_t)={KS_0,...,KS_t} -- 'exactly why provenance and immutable history matter.'

Works concrete examples for the four transition types: Correction (RAM figure corrected 16GB->32GB, same host/property/time, X was simply wrong); Change (Nexus version 3.69->3.8x after an upgrade, Correct(X,t1) and Correct(Y,t2) both hold, reality changed, essential for organizational memory); Refinement ('runs on RHEL' later refined to 'RHEL 9.8 on a specific VM using rootless Podman', greater resolution not falsification, Refinement!=Correction); Recontextualization ('the system is approved' meaning Approval_Architecture in one context vs Approval_Operations in another, X!=Y indicating different Context, not contradiction -- 'pure DDD territory'). States semantic transition typing must exceed a mere version number (v1 corrected_by v2, refined_by v3, superseded_by v4, valid_in Context-A) -- 'semantic transition > mere version number.'

States Step 184's verdict: 'an epistemic gap is a first-class state, not a defect to be hidden'; consolidates three protected non-identities: Inference!=Fact, Confidence!=Truth, Authorization!=Evidence. Requires the reconstruction model to include Established+Inferable+Unknown+Conflicted components, with Reconstruct(D) returning both reconstructed elements and Gap(D).

Requires EvidenceCondition for a decision to mean EvidenceRequirementSatisfied, not CompleteEvidence -- an authorized decision-maker can legitimately decide Proceed while E(p)=Unknown, with the record explicitly containing DecisionUnderUncertainty=True, rejecting the implicit assumption Unknown=>NoDecision as false. Expands the decision tuple to D=(DecisionContent,EvidenceState,Authority,Uncertainty,Rationale,Time,Context). Formalizes two separate, never-merged state machines: Epistemic (ES: Unknown->Observed->Supported->Determined with Conflict/Refuted/Superseded branches) and Authority (AS: None->Granted->Delegated->Expired/Revoked), intersecting at governance transitions only via DecisionAllowed=F(ES,AS,Rule).

Distinguishes six specific reasons a proposition can be Unknown -- NotObserved, NotRecorded, NotAccessible, Conflicted, NotEvaluated, Indeterminate -- worked example: Decision=Reject(B) with Rationale=NotRecorded is meaningfully different from Rationale=Conflicted or NotAccessible. Requires missing information to be represented explicitly (EpistemicStatus=Unknown, never a bare null/N/A/'probably X') and requires the reconstruction graph to show a literal [JUSTIFICATION NOT RECORDED] gap rather than an AI-filled plausible rationale (explicitly rejected architecture) -- 'narrative completeness must never outrank epistemic correctness'; preferring 'I cannot establish why' over 'the likely reason was...' specifically for historical-reconstruction tasks, while inference remains appropriate when a user explicitly requests plausible explanations (task semantics must be distinguished).

Mathematically confirms two prior findings: Unknown needs a reason field, formalized E(p)=(Unknown,UReason), directly supporting Step 184's Unknown typology; and validity-time/knowledge-time separation T=(T_valid,T_known) as a candidate invariant, worked through a concrete misconfiguration example (T_valid=[Jan,Mar), T_known=Mar; Reality=Misconfigured while OrganizationalKnowledge=Unknown during Jan-Feb).

Mathematically confirms two prior findings: Unknown needs a reason field, formalized E(p)=(Unknown,UReason), directly supporting Step 184's Unknown typology; and validity-time/knowledge-time separation T=(T_valid,T_known) as a candidate invariant, worked through a concrete misconfiguration example (T_valid=[Jan,Mar), T_known=Mar; Reality=Misconfigured while OrganizationalKnowledge=Unknown during Jan-Feb).

Discovers authority requires provenance just as knowledge does: AuthorityClaim=(Actor,Scope,Rule,Validity,Provenance), an assertion without its basis is epistemically incomplete. Formalizes delegation (Delegates(Board,A,x)=1 required for Auth(A,x)=1 under valid delegation constraints, requiring AuthorityEvidence, not a bare assertion). Confirms authority is temporal (only valid within an interval, connecting to Step 185's T_valid!=T_known) and contextual (Auth(A,r,C1)!=Auth(A,r,C2)), concluding authority is a relation Authority subseteq Actor x Action x Context x Time, not an intrinsic personal property.

Refines the temporal model to four timestamps per evidence item -- T_valid, T_observed, T_known, T_recorded -- worked through a four-date security-compromise example, noting a conventional created_at field loses this distinction. Concludes the semantic core only needs to be bitemporal (ValidTime, KnowledgeTime), with the other two timestamps potentially treated as provenance metadata rather than domain-model core -- 'we shouldn't put every timestamp into the domain model merely because mathematics allows it.'

Formalizes a typed version relation R(p_i,p_j) in {Change,Correction,Refinement,Supersession,Contradiction} (worked example: R(3.69,3.70)=Change vs R(3.69,3.68)=Correction if the original assertion was erroneous). Defines Replay(D,t0) as reconstructing K_t0/R_t0/A_t0 and asking whether D was admissible then -- explicitly not 'would we decide the same today?' -- distinguishing historical replay from counterfactual replay (Replay_counterfactual(D,t0,K_t1), a Pearl-style do-calculus question about later-knowledge-already-available), with ActualHistory != CounterfactualAnalysis, both representable but never confused.

Proposes a concrete five-case AI classification test (Correction/Real-world Change/Refinement/Recontextualization/Contradiction) requiring an AI agent to classify each transition and state what evidence would be required, with the diagnostic that failure to reliably distinguish the cases means the knowledge model is immature. States the success criterion: preserve HistoricalTruth without confusing it with CurrentTruth; preserve CurrentTruth without erasing HistoricalUncertainty; never promote Inference to Fact.

Formalizes Capability, Permission, Authority, Responsibility as four independent parameterized relations Cap(a,x), Perm(a,x,c,t), Auth(a,d,c,t), Resp(a,d,c,t), with worked examples (a DBA with write permission lacking approval authority; a board holding authority while a role holds operational responsibility). Explicitly rejects the implication chain Cap=>Perm=>Auth=>Resp as FALSE. Formalizes Auth(a,r,c,t)=f(Role,Scope,Delegation,Rule,t,c), with f belonging to the governance model, not the mathematical kernel.

Consolidates eight invariants I21-I28 promoted to 'strong candidate' status (Capability!=Permission; Permission!=Authority; Authority!=Responsibility; Authority is contextual and temporal; Authority requires provenance/basis; Evidence cannot manufacture authority; Statistical confidence cannot manufacture authority; Kernel enforces, does not originate, authority). Reframes KnowledgeOS a final time as 'a constitutional state-transition system for organizational epistemic and governance continuity', sitting across transitions preserving Identity+Time+Provenance+State+Witness+Lineage -- explicitly noted as still requiring testing.

Redefines the Kernel mathematically as 'Invariant Enforcement Boundary': a transition is allowed only if Preconditions(Transition)=True, stronger than 'the Kernel stores knowledge' or a database abstraction. Lists what the Kernel explicitly does NOT do: compute P(H|E) and declare truth, determine organizational/moral authority, interpret domain meaning, or judge semantic reasonableness of an inference -- it only verifies the declared transition contract. Formalizes two distinct functions: a domain-specific/intelligent semantic evaluator f_sem(E,p)->Assessment and a deterministic transition validator f_val(Assessment,r)->Allowed/Rejected, giving the pattern 'probabilistic reasoning -> deterministic admission gate', rated potentially one of the strongest foundations of the architecture.

Answers the central Step-186/187 question: KnowledgeOS cannot become the source of authority itself, expressed as Authority->GovernanceRule->TransitionContract->KnowledgeOS Enforcement, never KnowledgeOS->Authority. Consolidates a three-part separation-of-powers principle: Kernel enforces authority claims but does not originate authority; preserves epistemic status but does not originate truth; preserves decisions but does not originate organizational decisions -- formalized Source_Truth!=Kernel, Source_Authority!=Kernel, Source_Governance!=Kernel, with the Kernel redefined as EnforcementBoundary.

Defines the deterministic admission function Adm(r,a,K)=1 iff Preconditions(r,K) AND Permission(a,r) AND AuthorityRequirement(r,a) AND WitnessRequirement(r) -- the system judges only whether the declared constitutional contract is satisfied, never whether a decision was philosophically wise. Applies this decisively: even at P(H|E)=0.999, an AI's Auth(AI,ApproveDecision) remains 0 unless explicitly granted -- 'statistical confidence cannot manufacture authority', an extremely strong architectural invariant.

Formalizes Allowed(a,r) = Cap(a,r) AND Perm(a,r) AND AuthReq(r,a), requiring AuthReq(r) to be transition-specific (not every transition, e.g. an automated observation-recording, needs human authority). Enumerates seven transition classes (Record/Derive/Evaluate/Determine/Approve/Decide/Execute) with typically different authority requirements, conceptual not yet a fixed RACI. States the crucial reframing: ask 'is this actor authorized to cause THIS semantic transition in THIS context?', formalized Auth(a,r,c,t), rather than a coarse role check.

Formalizes a knowledge-transmission function tau:K_A->K_B where K_B does not automatically equal K_A, with four preservation properties (Pres_I identity, Pres_T temporal semantics, Pres_P provenance, Pres_M meaning), ideal transmission requiring all four jointly -- noted as potentially important for future AI knowledge-transfer modelling.

Models organizational knowledge as a stochastic-process-style filtration F_t0 subseteq F_t1 subseteq ... subseteq F_tn (information sets accumulate monotonically even as individual propositions' status can change), giving the rigorous decision constraint D_t=f(F_t,R_t,A_t), never f(F_{t+1},...) unless explicitly counterfactual -- 'a very strong mathematical foundation for our architecture.' States the Step-188 verdict: Decision_t=f(F_t,R_t,A_t) and F_t subseteq F_{t+1} as a useful information-theoretic abstraction, plus CurrentState!=HistoricalTrajectory and HistoricalDecision!=CounterfactualDecision, consolidating I29-I32 alongside I21-I28 into 'a surprisingly coherent mathematical constitution.'

Formalizes four new invariants: I29 no hindsight contamination (Evaluate(D_t)=f(D_t,K_t,R_t,A_t), never K_{t+n} unless explicitly counterfactual); I30 historical immutability (correction happens via a new transition Old--Correction-->New, never an overwrite Old<-New); I31 temporal causality (evidence acquired after a decision cannot be decision-time knowledge, unless the record explicitly shows it was already known but recorded later, distinguishing NotKnown from KnownButNotRecorded via T_known<T_recorded, explaining why provenance cannot reduce to createdAt); I32 knowledge accumulation does not imply monotonic certainty increase (entropy H(K_{t+1}) can exceed H(K_t) when new information reveals prior certainty was unjustified -- KnowledgeGrowth != CertaintyGrowth, letting an AI system legitimately move from Supported yesterday to Conflicted today as progress, not degradation).

Models organizational knowledge as a stochastic-process-style filtration F_t0 subseteq F_t1 subseteq ... subseteq F_tn (information sets accumulate monotonically even as individual propositions' status can change), giving the rigorous decision constraint D_t=f(F_t,R_t,A_t), never f(F_{t+1},...) unless explicitly counterfactual -- 'a very strong mathematical foundation for our architecture.' States the Step-188 verdict: Decision_t=f(F_t,R_t,A_t) and F_t subseteq F_{t+1} as a useful information-theoretic abstraction, plus CurrentState!=HistoricalTrajectory and HistoricalDecision!=CounterfactualDecision, consolidating I29-I32 alongside I21-I28 into 'a surprisingly coherent mathematical constitution.'

Also notes an equivalence relation needs transitivity to have a quotient at all, unestablished for equiv (semantic equality) and resolved only for cong_I within a context (I_48).
